MUTATION PROBES -- I deliberately broke what this PR asserts and relies on. All probes ran in an isolated copy of the repository under a scratch directory; the real checkout's working tree was verified clean (git status --porcelain empty) before and after.

PROBE A (does this record unblock the PR?). Added a schema-complete AGREE record alongside my prior DISAGREE one: still FAIL. A DISAGREE record in reviews/<pr>/ is a HARD BLOCK, not merely a record that fails to count -- worth knowing, and not something the README states. Replacing the DISAGREE record's contents with AGREE: "lwb-lanes check passed", EXIT=0. So this record, at this path, is what turns CI green.

PROBE B (the decisive one, and it overturned my own first reading). The document claims "This pull request is itself an instance" of the record-only bypass. I expected that to be FALSE now, because 5e415c44 touches HANDOFF.md, so resolve_reviewable_head returns 5e415c44 -- the PR's own head, not the base -- which I measured. I was about to file it as a finding. I tested it instead: I replaced the ENTIRE contents of reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md with a line of nonsense asserting the opposite of the document, committed it, and re-ran the gate with an unchanged AGREE record. Result: "lwb-lanes check passed", EXIT=0, reviewable head still 5e415c44. The claim is SUBSTANTIVELY TRUE, for a reason narrower than the one the document gives: the bypass is not about whether the PR as a whole is record-only, but about WHERE the content lives. Anything under reviews/ or proof/ can be changed by a record-only commit that never moves the reviewable head, no matter what else the PR touches. The document's operative warning -- "a green lwb-lanes here is not evidence that anything in this file was reviewed" -- is correct and I confirmed it by experiment.

PROBE C (is the freshness check vacuous in the other direction?). Appended one line to HANDOFF.md (a non-record path) and committed: reviewable head moved to the new sha and EVERY review record was correctly rejected as STALE, EXIT=1. So the binding is real for non-record content. Precise state at this head: HANDOFF.md's content IS bound to a review record; reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md's content is NOT. Both measured.

FINDINGS -- two. One blocking, one structural and not charged to this PR.

FINDING 1 (BLOCKING, and the reason for DISAGREE). proof/32.json marks a structurally unverifiable command as verifiable. scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute reports, in this repo's own words:

  FAIL: proof/32.json: python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py: self-referencing command is marked verifiable: true -- a proof record cannot claim its own re-execution as proof; mark it verifiable: false with an enum reason instead

This is not my inference; it is the repository's tooling naming the defect and stating the fix. I measured how every other record handles the same command: of the 20 numeric proof records, proof/32.json is the ONLY one that sets verifiable on a self-referencing lwb_check_proof invocation. All 16 prior instances across proof/7,8,9,10,11,13,15,16,17,18,19 omit the field entirely and are correctly reported as SKIPPED-SELF. So this is a one-record slip against an established house convention, not a disagreement about it.

The second mismatch in the same record is softer and I do not block on it alone: the recorded sha256 for `python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .` does not reproduce (recorded b46eda93..., re-run e73af850...), because the record was captured at 3509d2f and HANDOFF.md was regenerated afterwards in 5e415c44. Its recorded tail still shows the OLD block ("Generated: 2026-09-19 11:34 UTC", "19 record(s)"). That is the unavoidable cost of putting the generator last, which is the correct ordering; but the command is flagged verifiable: true, so the record asserts a reproducibility it does not have at its own head.

Why I treat this as blocking rather than a nit, stated so the author can weigh it and overrule me if they judge otherwise. It does NOT redden CI: the lwb-proof-reexecute step is continue-on-error by deliberate and well-argued design, and GitHub reports it as "success" on all six legs even though the step's own exit code is 1 -- I confirmed both. The merge gate is satisfied. So a reasonable person could land this. My reasons for blocking anyway: (a) a proof record is an evidence artifact, and "verifiable: true" on something that cannot be verified is an overclaim about evidence -- which is precisely the failure this entire pull request exists to correct, now occurring a third time, one level down; (b) this repository's own norm, argued at length in the document under review, is that a LANDED record must not be rewritten afterwards, so the window to fix this closes at merge and the malformed record becomes permanent, surfacing on every future --reexecute run; (c) the fix is one field plus an enum reason, and re-recording the state-claims command at the final head would clear the digest too. Blocking costs the author minutes now and saves a permanent artifact that contradicts the PR's own thesis.

FINDING 2 (STRUCTURAL; NOT charged to this PR -- scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py is untouched by this diff). The generated-block PR-listing check cannot distinguish "I checked and found nothing wrong" from "I could not check". PROBE E: a fabricated #99 passes, because an unresolvable PR sets any_unverifiable and the listing is waved through with an Info. The CI step runs `python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .` with no GH_TOKEN in its environment (I read ci.yml lines 182-184 and found no job- or step-level token), so in CI the listing is very likely never re-derived at all. To the script's credit it PRINTS "UNVERIFIABLE ... (no gh auth here)" rather than pretending, so the output is honest even though the exit code is not -- this is the good half of the hazard, not the bad half. I record it because this PR rewrites that exact block, and a reader should not take the green check as confirmation of it. I verified the block by hand instead; it is correct.

The substance of this pull request is good and I want to be unambiguous about that. The correction it makes is true and corroborated from inside the repository; the fix to my previous blocking finding is complete, accurate, and goes further than I asked by stating that honest reporting would NOT have blocked #27; the decision not to amend a landed record is right; the ordering trap is handled correctly; the second limitation is recorded faithfully and, as PROBE B showed, more accurately than my own first reading of it. I am blocking on one thing: the PR's own proof record asserts verifiable: true for a command that cannot be verified, this repository's own tooling says so in plain language and names the fix, it is the only one of 20 records to do it, and once merged the repo's own no-amendment norm makes it permanent. A pull request whose subject is a record that overclaimed should not land carrying a record that overclaims. Set that command's verifiable to false with an enum reason (matching how all 16 prior instances are handled), and re-record the state-claims digest at the final head if you want the second mismatch gone too, and I would expect the next reviewer to AGREE.
